title: Ways of walking
about: Collocations for walking: going on foot, going for a walk, a run or a stroll, a brisk walk, pacing up and down, picking your way, wandering aimlessly and striding confidently. Also walking phrases used about life: walks of life, making great strides, getting off on the wrong foot.

parts.title: Adjectives and adverbs associated with walking

items.pattern: go / get / travel (somewhere) on foot · go places on foot · within walking distance
items.meaning: walk somewhere instead of driving or taking a bus
items.example: The station is only ten minutes away, so we usually **go on foot**.
more: The old town is so small that it's best to explore it **on foot**.
When the buses were on strike, half the city **went** to work **on foot**.
items.watchOut: «Пішки» — on foot: прийменник on і однина foot. On feet — помилка. By foot іноді трапляється, але стандартно й найприродніше — on foot. Часто простіше сказати walk: I walk to work.

items.pattern: go for a walk (in the park / along the river) · go for a long / short walk · take the dog for a walk
items.meaning: walk somewhere for pleasure or exercise, not to get to a particular place
items.example: After Sunday lunch, we always **go for a walk** along the river.
more: It's finally stopped raining. Shall we **go for a walk**?
I **went for a long walk** to clear my head after the argument.
items.watchOut: «Піти погуляти» — go for a walk, а не make a walk і не go to a walk. Буває й go on a walk, але в Британії частіше go for a walk. «Вигуляти собаку» — take the dog for a walk або walk the dog. Go walking — радше «ходити в піші походи».

items.pattern: go for a stroll · take a stroll (a bit more written) · a stroll along / around / through sth · verb: stroll
items.meaning: a slow, relaxed walk for pleasure
items.example: On warm evenings, the whole village **goes for a stroll** along the seafront.
more: Let's **take a stroll** round the garden while the kettle boils.
We **went for a stroll** through the market and ended up buying far too much cheese.
items.watchOut: У розмові частіше go for a stroll; take a stroll звучить трохи книжніше. Не make a stroll і не walk for a stroll. Stroll — це завжди повільно й без поспіху.

items.pattern: go running / jogging / swimming / cycling · go running in the park / on the beach
items.meaning: run for exercise, as a regular activity or on a particular occasion
items.example: My neighbour **goes running** in the park every morning, whatever the weather.
more: Do you want to **go running** with me tomorrow morning?
I **went running** for the first time in years and could hardly walk the next day.
items.watchOut: Заняття на -ing ставлять після go: go running, go swimming, go shopping. Не make running, не go to running і не go for running.

items.pattern: go for a run / a jog / a swim · go for a quick / long run · break into a run = suddenly start running
items.meaning: go out and run once, for exercise
items.example: I'm going to **go for a run** before it gets dark.
more: When I'm stressed, I **go for a long run** and forget about everything.
She **went for a quick run** round the block to wake herself up.
items.watchOut: «Піти на пробіжку» — go for a run, а не make a run і зазвичай не take a run. Make a run for it — це інше: «кинутися тікати».

items.pattern: a brisk walk · go for / take / have a brisk walk · at a brisk pace
items.meaning: a walk at a fast, energetic speed
items.example: The doctor told Dad to **take a brisk walk** every day for his heart.
more: Half an hour's **brisk walk** in the cold air woke me up completely.
A **brisk walk** gets you to the station in ten minutes; if you stroll, it's twenty.
items.watchOut: Brisk /brɪsk/ — швидкий, енергійний. Не плутай із brusque /bruːsk/ — різкий, грубуватий (про манеру людини). A quick walk — частіше «коротка прогулянка», не обов'язково швидка.

items.pattern: pace up and down (sth) · pace (around) the room · pace the floor
items.meaning: walk backwards and forwards in a small space, usually because you are nervous, worried or impatient
items.example: While we waited for news from the hospital, Dad **paced up and down** the kitchen.
more: Stop **pacing up and down**! You're making me nervous.
The dog **paced up and down** by the door, waiting for the children to come home from school.
items.watchOut: «Ходити туди-сюди» — pace up and down або walk up and down; pace підкреслює хвилювання чи нетерпіння. Не go here and there і не step up and down: here and there — «тут і там», про місця, а не про рух.

items.pattern: take a step / steps · take a few / long / small steps · take a step forward / back
items.meaning: move your feet to walk a short distance; long steps cover a lot of ground each time
items.example: After his knee operation, Grandad could only **take a few steps** without his stick.
more: **Take** two **steps** back so I can get everyone in the photo.
My husband **takes** such **long steps** that I have to hurry to keep up.
items.watchOut: «Зробити крок» — take a step, а не do a step. Make a step у прямому значенні звучить як калька. «Іти широкими кроками» — take long steps або stride.

items.pattern: It's an easy walk (to / into sth) (from here) · a gentle walk along / around sth · go for a gentle walk
items.meaning: an easy walk is neither long nor difficult; a gentle walk is slow and relaxed, without hills or hard effort
items.uk: недалеко й неважко пройти пішки (easy); неспішна, неважка прогулянка (gentle)
items.example: The beach is **an easy walk** from the campsite, about ten minutes along a flat path.
more: After her operation, Mum could only manage **a gentle walk** round the garden.
On Sunday we did **a gentle walk** by the lake, perfect for the grandchildren.
items.watchOut: «Легка прогулянка» — an easy walk або a gentle walk; калька a light walk звучить незвично. «Звідси недалеко пішки» — It's an easy walk from here або It's a short walk from here.

items.pattern: heavy / light steps · heavy / light footsteps · walk with heavy / light steps
items.meaning: heavy steps are slow and loud (the person is big, or tired, sad or angry); light steps are quick and quiet
items.example: I heard Dad's **heavy steps** on the stairs and knew he'd had a bad day.
more: She danced into the kitchen with **light steps**, humming her favourite song.
Our upstairs neighbour walks with such **heavy steps** that the lamp shakes.

items.pattern: a leisurely / gentle stroll · go for / take a leisurely stroll (along / around / through sth)
items.meaning: a slow, relaxed walk with no hurry at all
items.example: On our last evening in Rome, we went for **a leisurely stroll** through the old streets.
more: After Sunday lunch, the whole family takes **a gentle stroll** to the park.
It's not a race. It's **a leisurely stroll**, so slow down!
items.watchOut: Leisurely /ˈleʒəli/ — прикметник, хоч і закінчується на -ly: a leisurely stroll, a leisurely breakfast. Не a leisure stroll.

items.pattern: walk briskly / swiftly (over to / towards / along sth) · move swiftly
items.meaning: walk quickly and with energy
items.example: It was freezing, so we **walked briskly** to keep warm.
more: The waiter **walked swiftly** between the tables with a tray of drinks.
Late for her train, she **walked briskly** along the platform.
items.watchOut: Briskly і swiftly часто вживають замість quickly, коли йдеться про ходу. Не плутай briskly з brusquely — «різко, грубувато».

items.pattern: pick your way (cautiously / carefully) across / along / through / over sth
items.meaning: walk slowly and carefully across a difficult or dangerous place, choosing where to put your feet
items.example: We **picked our way cautiously** across the rocks to the edge of the water.
more: She **picked her way** through the toys on the bedroom floor.
After the storm, we **picked our way carefully** over the fallen branches.
items.watchOut: Pick your way — не «вибрати свій шлях» у житті, а обережно пробиратися. Займенник збігається з підметом: I picked my way, they picked their way.

items.pattern: wander (aimlessly) around / round / through / along sth · wander about
items.meaning: walk slowly with no clear plan or purpose
items.example: On my first day in Lisbon, I **wandered aimlessly** through the narrow streets and loved every minute.
more: Teenagers **wander aimlessly** round the shopping centre on Saturday afternoons.
On holiday I love to **wander aimlessly** around markets, just looking at things.
items.watchOut: Wander /ˈwɒndə/ — блукати, тинятися. Не плутай із wonder /ˈwʌndə/ — цікавитися, дивуватися: пишуться й вимовляються по-різному.

items.pattern: stride confidently / angrily / purposefully into / across / out of sth · stride – strode – stridden · take confident / angry / purposeful strides
items.meaning: walk with long, firm steps in a confident, angry or determined way
items.uk: іти широким кроком — упевнено, сердито, рішуче
items.example: The new head teacher **strode confidently** onto the stage and smiled at everyone.
more: My brother **strode angrily** out of the room and slammed the door.
The ticket inspector **strode purposefully** down the train towards us.
items.watchOut: Минулий час — strode: She strode into the room. Stride — це довгі, рішучі кроки; для обережної ходи кажуть pick your way, для неспішної — stroll.

items.pattern: walk it · walk an exam / a test (informal, mostly British) · walk it = also win very easily
items.meaning: pass an exam or test very easily, or succeed or win without any difficulty
items.uk: скласти (іспит) з легкістю, пройти як по маслу
items.example: Don't worry about your driving test. You'll **walk it**.
more: My cousin was top of her year and **walked** every exam she sat.
'How did the interview go?' 'I **walked it**. They offered me the job on the spot.'
items.watchOut: Розмовне, переважно британське. У walk it є й пряме значення — «дійти пішки»: The taxi didn't come, so we walked it. Що мається на увазі, підкаже контекст.

items.pattern: a walking encyclopaedia (UK spelling; US encyclopedia) · a walking dictionary
items.meaning: a person who knows a lot of facts about many things
items.example: Ask Grandad about plants: he's **a walking encyclopaedia**.
more: When it comes to dinosaurs, my nephew is **a walking encyclopaedia**.
We always want Tom on our quiz team. He's **a walking encyclopaedia**.
items.watchOut: Тут англійська збігається з українською. Пастки — написання й наголос: британське encyclopaedia, американське encyclopedia; наголос на -pae-.

items.pattern: run into problems / difficulties / trouble · also run up against problems · compare: run into sb = meet by chance
items.meaning: start to have problems, often unexpectedly
items.example: We **ran into problems** with the car halfway to the coast.
more: The builders **ran into difficulties** when they found an old well under the kitchen.
If you **run into trouble** with the homework, give me a call.
items.watchOut: «Зіткнутися з проблемами» — run into problems / difficulties, а не collide with problems. Run into sb — це інше: випадково зустріти когось (I ran into my old teacher in town).

items.pattern: people from all / different walks of life · from every walk of life
items.meaning: different jobs, social positions and backgrounds
items.uk: люди різних професій і верств, з усіх верств суспільства
items.example: Our choir has members from **all walks of life**: a bus driver, a nurse, a retired judge.
more: Volunteers from **different walks of life** helped to clean up the beach.
The marathon attracts runners from **every walk of life**.
items.watchOut: Walk of life — не «прогулянка життям» і не «життєвий шлях», а професія чи становище в суспільстві. Зазвичай у множині й з from: from all walks of life.

items.pattern: rush headlong into sth / doing sth · rush headlong into marriage / a decision · also run / dive headlong into sth
items.meaning: start doing something too quickly, without thinking carefully first
items.uk: кидатися стрімголов (необачно) у щось, поспіхом за щось братися
items.example: They'd only known each other a month, so their parents begged them not to **rush headlong into** marriage.
more: Don't **rush headlong into** buying a house. Look at a few more first.
I **rushed headlong into** a new job and regretted it within a week.
items.watchOut: Rush headlong into — завжди про необачність і поспіх. Українське «кинутися з головою в роботу» (захопитися) — це радше throw yourself into your work.

items.pattern: take your first faltering / tentative / careful steps (in / towards / as sth) · take the first step
items.meaning: begin to do something new, carefully and without much confidence yet
items.example: After moving to Canada, Anna **took her first faltering steps** in French.
more: Our little café is **taking its first faltering steps**, but customers are starting to come back.
At sixty, Dad **took his first tentative steps** as a painter.
items.watchOut: «Робити перші кроки» — take your first steps, з take, а не do. Faltering /ˈfɔːltərɪŋ/ — хиткий, невпевнений; tentative і careful steps кажуть, коли людина робить щось обережно й без упевненості.

items.pattern: make great / huge / enormous strides (in / with sth) · make strides towards sth · less often: take great strides
items.meaning: make a lot of progress; improve quickly
items.uk: досягати великих успіхів, робити великий поступ, швидко прогресувати
items.example: After three months of physio, Dad has **made great strides**: he can climb the stairs again.
more: My daughter has **made great strides** with the piano this year.
The town has **made huge strides** in cleaning up the river.
items.watchOut: «Досягати великих успіхів» — make great strides або make great progress, а не make great successes. Progress — незлічуваний: не a progress і не progresses. «Великі кроки» в переносному значенні — great strides.

items.pattern: run up against opposition / problems / difficulties · also come up against sth · strong / fierce opposition
items.meaning: suddenly have to deal with people who disagree with you, or with difficulties
items.example: The plan to close the village school **ran up against** strong **opposition** from parents.
more: When I suggested moving to the country, I **ran up against** some **opposition** from the kids.
The new parking rules have **run up against** a lot of **opposition** from shop owners.
items.watchOut: Opposition тут — не лише політична опозиція, а будь-який опір, незгода людей. «Наштовхнутися на опір» — run up against або come up against opposition: усі три слова йдуть разом.

items.phrase: get off on the wrong foot
items.pattern: get off / start off on the wrong foot (with sb) · opposite: get off on the right foot
items.meaning: start a relationship badly
items.example: I arrived late on my first day and **got off on the wrong foot** with my boss.
more: Our new neighbours parked across our drive on their first day, so we **got off on the wrong foot**.
Let's forget about yesterday. I think we **got off on the wrong foot**.
items.watchOut: Не плутай з українським «встати не з тієї ноги» — це про поганий настрій зранку: get out of bed on the wrong side. Get off on the wrong foot — погано почати стосунки з кимось.

warmup.uk: Ми зазвичай ходимо на роботу пішки.
warmup.q: We usually go to work on ___.
warmup.explain: Пішки — on foot, в однині. On feet і on legs — помилки.

warmup.q: Let's ___ for a walk in the park!
warmup.explain: Піти погуляти — go for a walk. Make a walk — калька.

warmup.uk: Швидка прогулянка — найкращі ліки від сонливості.
warmup.q: A ___ walk is the best cure for sleepiness.
warmup.explain: Швидка, бадьора прогулянка — a brisk walk. Brusque — різкий, грубуватий (про манеру людини).

warmup.uk: Він нервово ходив туди-сюди по кімнаті.
warmup.q: He was nervously ___ up and down the room.
warmup.explain: Ходити туди-сюди від хвилювання — pace up and down.
Зробити крок — take a step. Make a step і do a step — кальки.

warmup.uk: Моя донька склала всі іспити без жодних зусиль.
warmup.explain: Розмовне walk an exam / walk it — скласти іспит дуже легко.

warmup.uk: За рік занять він досяг великих успіхів в англійській.
warmup.q: After a year of lessons, he has made great ___ in English.
warmup.explain: Досягти великих успіхів — make great strides (або make great progress). Successes тут не підходить.

warmup.uk: Я невдало почав стосунки з новим тренером.
warmup.q: I got off on the wrong ___ with my new coach.
warmup.explain: Get off on the wrong foot — погано почати стосунки. «Встати не з тієї ноги» — інше: get out of bed on the wrong side.

A.q: It was a warm evening, so after dinner we ___ for a stroll by the lake.
A.explain: Прогулятися — go for a stroll або take a stroll (без for). Make a stroll — калька.

A.q: The football coach ___ up and down the touchline for the whole match.
A.explain: Ходити туди-сюди від хвилювання — pace up and down.
Бігати для здоров'я — go running. Make і take тут не вживають.

B.q: The station is just down the hill, so it's ___ walk even with heavy bags.
B.explain: Недалеко й неважко пройти — an easy walk. A light walk так зазвичай не кажуть.

B.q: With no plans for the afternoon, we just wandered ___ around the old town.
B.explain: Wander aimlessly — безцільно блукати. Purposefully — цілеспрямовано, briskly — швидко, а тут немає ні мети, ні поспіху.

B.q: Annoyed by the long queue, the man ___ angrily up to the counter.
B.explain: Stride — іти широким рішучим кроком, часто сердито чи впевнено. Stroll і wander — повільно й спокійно.

C.q: The school trip ___ into problems when half the class got ill.
C.explain: Зіткнутися з проблемами — run into problems.

C.q: Our local gym has members from all ___ of life.
C.explain: Люди різних професій і верств — people from all walks of life.

C.q: Think carefully before you sign. Don't ___ headlong into anything.
C.explain: Rush headlong into sth — кидатися стрімголов, необачно.

example.title: Grandad gets fit
example.uk:
Минулої весни дідусь вирішив покращити свою фізичну форму. Спочатку він міг зробити лише кілька кроків без відпочинку, але ні в що не кидався стрімголов. Щоранку він виходив на неспішну прогулянку парком, а невдовзі ця прогулянка стала швидкою й бадьорою.

До літа він досяг великих успіхів. Він вступив до клубу любителів піших прогулянок, де були люди найрізніших професій і верств, але невдало почав знайомство з керівницею: сказав їй, що її маршрут задовгий.

Під час першого походу з клубом дідусь обережно пробрався через багнисте поле, а потім упевнено, широким кроком рушив угору на пагорб попереду всіх. Тепер він скрізь ходить пішки, а керівниця називає його ходячою енциклопедією: він знає кожну стежку в околицях.

Last spring, Grandad decided to get fit. At first he could only [[take a few steps|a8]] without a rest, but he didn't [[rush headlong into|c5]] anything. Every morning he went for [[a gentle walk|b1]] round the park, and soon it became [[a brisk walk|a6]].

By summer he had [[made great strides|c7]]. He joined a walking club with people from [[all walks of life|c4]], but he [[got off on the wrong foot|c9]] with the leader by telling her that her route was too long.

On his first trip with the club, Grandad [[picked his way|b5]] across a muddy field and then [[strode confidently|b7]] up the hill, ahead of everyone. Now he goes everywhere [[on foot|a1]], and the leader calls him a [[walking encyclopaedia|c2]]: he knows every path in the area.
